html:
The Ngadju, or Ngadjumaya, are an Aboriginal people of the Goldfields and Esperance region of Western Australia, in country around present day Norseman and inland from Esperance.

Their land lies in the Great Western Woodlands, a huge area of eucalyptus woodland between the wheatbelt and the Nullarbor. Neighbours on the map include the Wudjari on the coast, the Mirning to the east and the Kalaako to the north. Their language belongs to the Pama-Nyungan family.

The gold rushes of the 1890s brought miners and towns into Ngadju country. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. For the wider story, see Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Ngadju, or Ngadjumaya, are an Aboriginal people of the Goldfields and Esperance region of Western Australia, in country around present day Norseman and inland from Esperance.
